Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

multiGGM 0.10.0

Within-group edge rules and masking

  • select_edges(rule = "shrinkage") (mGHS): E[1 - kappa], where kappa is the edge’s shrinkage factor in its column update with the global scale included (new edge_probs() columns mean_shrinkage, p_shrinkage, mcse_shrinkage). It ranks edges as well as the paper’s E[w], but, like E[w] > 0.5, its 0.5 rule does not control false edges (better than E[w] at p = 20, n = 100; worse at p = 8, n = 300). For selection with error control use the magnitude rule.
  • select_edges(rule = "interval", level = 0.5): the credible interval excludes zero, the graphical horseshoe’s published rule (Li, Craig & Bhadra 2019), for comparison. edge_probs() group rows now have p_sign for every sampler.
  • New mask_pcor(): posterior mean partial correlations with unselected edges set to zero, for reporting each group’s network (not for finding differences, which should use select_diff_edges()).
  • calibrate_c() falls back to the raw share when fewer than three permutations make a call (c_method = "empirical").
  • All of the above is kept as running sums without random draws: chains are unchanged for a given seed.

Preparing for CRAN

  • Vignettes build in about 1.5 minutes instead of 12 (shorter illustrative chains; the tutorial’s multi-chain section uses SSVS), and the multiggm_mcmc() example is shorter.
  • DESCRIPTION: references with DOIs, acronyms spelled out.
  • Removed an unused C++ function.

multiGGM 0.9.0

  • New calibrate_c() chooses the minimum-difference threshold c for the magnitude rule (select_diff_edges(rule = "magnitude")) from a permutation null. The two groups’ labels are shuffled (group sizes kept, each original group centred on its own means, nothing rescaled), each shuffled dataset is refitted with the analysis settings, and every call it makes is false.
    • Default target: at most alpha of null datasets with any call, which is the FDR of the rule under the null. c is the (1 - alpha) quantile of a censored Weibull fitted to each permutation’s largest c with a call, so 20 to 50 permutations suffice. In permutation studies (SSVS, p = 10-30, n = 70-400 per group) the c chosen from 20 permutations gave an achieved null rate of 0.02-0.05 (target 0.05). target = "mean_false_calls" is also available.
    • Settings come from the analysis fit (fit =) or mcmc_args; failed fits are recorded and skipped; permutations are reproducible and identical in parallel; early stopping when the confidence interval for c is within c_tol.
    • print(), plot() and as.data.frame() methods.
  • select_diff_edges() accepts the result of calibrate_c() as c.
  • multiggm_mcmc() records its settings in fit$settings (not read by the samplers), so they can be reused. For older fits calibrate_c() reconstructs them, asking for burnin when it cannot be recovered.
  • Fine c grids need no change: diff_deltas (any grid, both scales) has worked for every sampler since 0.5.0. At p = 100, a 40-value grid takes about 28 MB of running sums (16 MB with mcse_batches = 0) and adds about 10% to run time.
  • Edge-selection vignette: new section on choosing c from a permutation null.

multiGGM 0.8.0

mGHS: small-sample failures and an optional prior on R

  • Diagnosis. With few observations per group (for example K = 2, n = 100, p = 28 on TCGA data, or simulated data with n = 100), mGHS chains stopped with “global-scale parameter above 1e6”. The global scales tau were finite. The correlation of edge scales across groups, R, ran to +-1, so 1 - R12^2 went to 0 and the global-scale parameters, which divide by it, crossed the guard. This is a property of the posterior under the paper’s uniform prior on R, not a numerical error: the per-group local scales can align the groups’ scaled edges, and with small n the null edges’ signs are free, so only concordant strong edges inform R and they favour +-1. Rescaling all groups by a common constant did not help; n = 1000 per group did.
  • New hyper$R_eta (mGHS): an LKJ(eta) prior on R, pi(R) propto |R|^(eta - 1). The default, 1, is the paper’s uniform prior and leaves the sampler unchanged (default fits are bit-identical to 0.7.0, tested at p = 50, n = 1000). On the TCGA example, eta = 5 and eta = 10 ran 20,000 + 20,000 iterations on 2 chains for all 5 seeds with R-hat <= 1.01 for tau and R; eta = 3 failed in 8 of 10 chains.
  • The error for a chain stuck at the boundary of R now says so and points to R_eta; a stuck chain reports stuck_mu. A warning is given when a chain had to be restarted, since restarted chains report only runs that avoided the failure.

multiGGM 0.7.0

  • New posterior_predictive_check() and plot_ppc(). Replicate data are drawn from posterior precision draws with the observed group sizes and compared with the data, giving posterior predictive p-values:
    • per group: dependence strength (max_abs_cor, sum_sq_cor), and outliers and heavy tails (max_mahal, kurtosis, as realized discrepancies);
    • per pair of groups: the total difference between groups (sum_sq_diff), which shows whether differences are over-shrunk;
    • per edge: each group’s sample partial correlation (or correlation) and its difference between groups. Works for G-Wishart, SSVS and mGHS. It needs saved draws (thinning to about 200 is enough); use = "mean" gives an approximate check for fits without draws. Runs in R after fitting, so chains are unaffected.
  • The “Checking and Evaluating a Fit” vignette gains a section on posterior predictive checks.

To do

  • Edge probabilities, diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for method = "ssvs_platform" (currently an error).

multiGGM 0.6.0

Diagnostics and evaluation without saving draws

Everything below works with save_draws = FALSE for the G-Wishart, SSVS and mGHS samplers. The samplers keep the extra traces and running sums without drawing random numbers, so chains and all existing outputs are unchanged for a given seed (tested against 0.4.0 and 0.5.0).

  • Convergence. New mcmc_diagnostics() reports rank-normalized split R-hat and bulk/tail ESS (Vehtari et al. 2021) for whole-chain summaries recorded at every iteration (fit$trace): edges per group, differential edges per pair (structural, |D| > c, union), the log-likelihood of each group, and theta (mGHS: R, tau). It also reports the Monte Carlo error of edge probabilities, the largest disagreement between chains and the acceptance rates, with flags. New plot_chain_agreement() plots each chain’s edge probabilities against chain 1.
  • plot_trace() gains "loglik" and "diff" and now works without saved draws and for mGHS ("edges" counts edges with w > 0.5). edge_counts() uses the trace when draws were not saved.
  • Monte Carlo SEs of edge probabilities. Every count used for selection is also kept in batches (mcse_batches, default 20); edge_probs() gains mcse_struct, mcse_cut, mcse_exceed_<c> and mcse_union_<c>, pooled correctly over chains.
  • Direction of differences. edge_probs() gains p_up_<c> = P(D > c) and p_down_<c> = P(D < -c).
  • Node level. New node_diff_summary(): per node, the posterior mean number of differential edges, the probability of at least one, and the rewiring score sum_j |D_ij|, all counted per iteration.
  • Network level. New diff_count_posterior(): the posterior of the number of differential edges and P(at least one).
  • q-values. New bfdr_qvalues(); the edge tables of select_edges() and select_diff_edges() gain a q_value column.
  • Prior versus posterior. New prior_only = TRUE samples the prior (G-Wishart and SSVS; mGHS’s flat diagonal prior is improper), and edge_bayes_factors() compares each edge probability with its prior value.
  • WAIC. New waic = TRUE keeps per-observation sums and compute_waic() returns WAIC with standard errors, overall and per group.
  • Calibration. New fdr_calibration() compares the posterior expected FDR with the achieved FDR and power against a known truth, for simulation studies.
  • New vignette “Checking and Evaluating a Fit”.
  • Cost: no measurable change in run time at p = 100 (SSVS and mGHS, with or without WAIC). The batch counts roughly double edge_acc (an SSVS fit without draws grows from 2.7 to 4.9 MB at p = 100, K = 2; set mcse_batches = 0 to drop them). The traces are a few numbers per iteration.

multiGGM 0.5.0

Posterior edge probabilities without saving draws

  • Every sampler except "ssvs_platform" now keeps running sums over all post-burn-in iterations (fit$edge_acc) for a common family of per-edge posterior probabilities. Each is counted per iteration and averaged, never assembled from the groups’ marginal summaries. They do not draw random numbers: chains, and every existing output, are unchanged for a given seed (mGHS outputs are bit-identical to 0.4.0; tested).
    • Per group: posterior mean and SD (precision and partial correlation), P(|x| > c), and the structural probability: the PIP for G-Wishart and SSVS; for mGHS P(w > 0.5) and E[w] with w = lambda^2/(1 + lambda^2), plus the cut-model P(Z = 1).
    • Per pair of groups: P(G_s != G_t) (mGHS: P(S_s != S_t) and P(Z_s != Z_t)), P(|D| > c), the union P(structural difference or |D| > c), the mean and SD of D, and the sign probability (labelled as not a probability of difference).
  • New edge_probs() (tidy data frame), edge_prob_matrix() (one p x p matrix) and select_edges() (per-group selection, rules "structural", "magnitude", "cut", "median_shrinkage").
  • select_diff_edges() gains rules "union" and "cut", a decision argument ("bfdr" or "median") and c (alias of delta, whose default is unchanged). The structural rule now also works for mGHS (it used to stop with an error) and for fits without saved draws.
  • save_draws = FALSE now works for the G-Wishart and SSVS samplers too: only the running sums, posterior means and the Theta trace are kept, which makes fits at p = 100-250 practical. pip_edges(), pip_diff_edge(), coef(), fitted(), diff_summary() and summary() use the running sums when draws are missing.
  • diff_deltas (the thresholds c) applies to every sampler. Thresholds outside the grid can be computed after fitting when draws were saved.
  • bayes_fdr() keeps tied probabilities together: the cutoff falls only between distinct values.
  • The G-Wishart engine no longer allocates three unused draw-sized arrays.
  • Documented (not changed): mGHS’s structural and cut-model probabilities are weak for null edges, because the paper’s weight w excludes the global scale tau and the upstream cut model draws Z ~ Bernoulli(Phi(w - t)) rather than the paper’s closed form. Use the magnitude rule for mGHS.

Shared tools: ggmtools

  • precision_to_pcor(), confusion_at_threshold(), roc_auc() and plot_roc() now come from the new package ggmtools and are re-exported. spikeyglass re-exports the same functions, so attaching both packages no longer gives conflicting versions.
  • roc_auc() now handles tied scores correctly. The previous version accumulated one edge at a time in sorted order, so tied edges (e.g. PIPs of exactly 0 or 1) were ordered by matrix position. That made the AUC depend on variable order and could bias it by several hundredths. The curve now steps only at distinct scores, and the AUC equals the Mann-Whitney statistic. With no tied scores, the AUC is unchanged.
  • roc_auc() returns NA for auc (instead of an error) when the truth has no edges or no non-edges.
  • confusion_at_threshold() returns a list (was a named numeric vector) with precision and F1 added, and its third argument is now called threshold (was thr), with default 0.5. Use cm$TPR rather than cm["TPR"]. plot_recovery() returns these lists.
  • plot_roc() now uses base graphics and returns the ROC list invisibly (it previously returned a ggplot object). It gains add = TRUE to overlay curves.
  • precision_to_pcor() returns a matrix of NA with a warning (instead of an error) for a non-positive diagonal, and keeps dimnames.
  • New methods for the ggmtools generics pip_table() (PIPs as a long edge table) and pcor_estimate() (posterior-mean partial correlations, one matrix per group). Scripts written with these work on spikeyglass fits too.

Bug fixes

  • SSVS and multi-platform samplers: the spike-and-slab update of the graph similarity theta (inherited from the Matlab reference) drew its proposal with beta_prop as a scale but used it as a rate in the acceptance ratio, and had the sign of the (alpha - alpha_prop) * log(theta) term reversed for spike-to-slab moves. The platform similarity Phi had the same sign error and mixed scale and rate in its normalizing terms. The ratios are now computed from explicit gamma densities (as the G-Wishart sampler already did). Default SSVS fits are essentially unchanged (beta_prop = 1, w = 0.9); fits with smaller w, beta_prop != 1, or the multi-platform sampler will differ. beta_prop is now a rate for every sampler.
  • A partial hyper list no longer wipes out the other defaults for the G-Wishart and SSVS samplers. Unknown hyperparameter names are now an error.
  • simulate_multiggm(K = 1) returned two groups.
  • simulate_multiggm_platform() now shares one base graph across platforms (it drew an independent graph per platform); the data-generating process is documented, and the base and platform graphs are returned.

Changes

  • pip_edges(), pip_diff_edge(), posterior_pcor() and posterior_precision() now pool all chains by default (chain = NULL), like diff_summary() and select_diff_edges(); chain = i selects one.
  • New summary(), coef(), fitted() and plot() methods for multi-chain fits (multiggm_fit_list).
  • method = "ssvs_platform" now stops when nchains > 1 and warns that parallel is ignored, instead of silently running one chain.
  • Removed ineffective EIGEN_USE_BLAS / EIGEN_USE_LAPACKE defines from the mGHS sources (no change to results).
  • Repository and CRAN hygiene: compiled objects untracked, old demo moved to dev/, Depends: R (>= 4.0.0), BugReports, ASCII-only sources.
  • New tests for each fix, plus reproducibility tests (same seed, parallel versus serial, R versus C++ engine).

multiGGM 0.4.0

New features

  • multiggm_mcmc(method = "mghs") fits the multiple graphical horseshoe (Busatto & Stingo 2025), adapted from github.com/cbusatto/mGHS. It returns a multiggm_fit, so coef(), fitted(), posterior_pcor(), posterior_ci(), diff_prob_pcor(), plot_trace("theta") and multi-chain fitting work. It reproduces upstream’s draws exactly for the same seed (inst/mghs/VALIDATION.md). Local fixes: rejection samplers that could hang, stuck checks that missed NaN, and a cut-model indexing bug (inst/mghs/UPSTREAM.md). New options: thin, save_draws = FALSE (keep only running summaries), automatic restart of stuck chains.
  • diff_draws(), diff_summary(), bayes_fdr() and select_diff_edges() for differential edges between any two groups, pooling chains by default. select_diff_edges() controls the posterior expected FDR using P(|D| > delta) (all samplers) or P(g_k != g_m) (G-Wishart and SSVS).

Changes

  • pip_edges(), pip_diff_edge() and edge_counts() stop with an explanatory error for mGHS fits, which have no edge indicators.
  • print() no longer reads adj_save to count draws for mGHS fits.
